title: Opening any client page swallows the whole staff sidebar — and employees have no way to get it back
surface: Staff sidebar, everywhere after visiting /clients/[id] (any sub-route)
whatYouSee: An employee clicks a client from the Clients grid. The sidebar instantly stops showing Clients, Agents, Jobs, Meetings, Assets, Calendar, Tasks, Connect and Analytics, and shows only four client tabs (Dashboard / AI Agents / Calendar / Workspace). A client copilot panel also appears on the right, uninvited. There is no close control and no "back to workspace" link. The nav stays that way as they keep clicking around. The only escapes are the logo — which lands on the staff dashboard with a sidebar still showing the four client tabs and nothing highlighted — or a full browser reload of a non-client page.
whyItsWrong: Nobody asked to enter client view — merely opening a client page seeds it, because the nested client layout mounts the context sync for all staff, employees included. The nav swap is keyed on staff-or-not, but the only control that clears the context lives inside the admin-only client picker at the bottom of the rail. So for every employee this is a one-way door, escapable only by a full page reload. The context is deliberately built to persist across navigation, which makes the trap sticky rather than transient.

src/app/(app)/clients/[id]/layout.tsx:36 — ClientContextSync mounted unconditionally for staff

fix: In src/components/sidebar.tsx: (a) move ClientContextPicker out of the `user.role === "KAROS_ADMIN"` guard at line 435 so employees get the same labelled exit, or add an always-visible "← Back to workspace" row above the client tabs inside `clientSections` (line 356) that calls setActiveClient(null) and routes to /clients — the same body as clearClient at lines 79-85; (b) better, stop swapping the nav wholesale at line 314 — keep adminItems and render clientViewNav(activeClient.client.id) as a labelled sub-group under the client header in clientSections, so no staff member can lose the workspace nav at all.

title: An approved user is never told they were approved; the pending screen is a static dead end
whatYouSee: "Awaiting approval — your account dh@example.com is registered as a client for Acme. An agency admin needs to approve it…" and one Sign out button. That is the entire screen. It never updates. When an admin approves the account minutes later, nothing happens: no email, no notification, no page change — the user has to guess and reload. If the admin rejects them, their account and sign-in record are deleted and they are told nothing; their next sign-in attempt simply fails.
whyItsWrong: The approve and reject actions flip the flags and revalidate the Team page; neither sends mail — the file imports no email helper at all — nor writes any notification, even though Resend is wired up and used elsewhere for support mail and deliveries. The pending page has no polling either, although a small auto-refresh component already exists in the codebase for exactly this pattern, and the page already redirects to the workspace as soon as the account is enabled. There is also no support link on the screen, so a user stuck here has no in-product way to ask what is happening — and this is the very first impression the portal makes on a new client.
evidence: src/app/pending/page.tsx:9 — already redirects to /dashboard the moment the account is enabled, so a refresh is all that is missing
src/app/pending/page.tsx:31 — LogoutButton is the only control on the page
src/lib/actions/user-actions.ts:13 — the import block pulls in data + auth + adminAuth only; no email helper
src/lib/actions/user-actions.ts:112 — approveRegistrationAction ends at revalidatePath("/team"); no mail, no notification
src/lib/actions/user-actions.ts:118 — rejectRegistrationAction deletes the Firestore doc and the auth account silently
src/components/auto-refresh.tsx:11 — AutoRefresh(intervalMs) already exists
src/lib/email.ts:16 — sendEmail via Resend, soft-failing, ready to use
fix: Three additions. (1) In src/lib/actions/user-actions.ts, after the upsert at line 110 send a Resend mail with sendEmail from src/lib/email.ts ("You're in — sign in here"), and a neutral decline mail in rejectRegistrationAction before the delete at line 118 (capture the email first); reuse the existing emailShell helper for markup. (2) In src/app/pending/page.tsx mount `<AutoRefresh intervalMs={15000} />` from src/components/auto-refresh.tsx — the existing redirect at line 9 then flips the user into the workspace with no manual reload. (3) Add an expected-timeframe line and a support mailto beside the Sign out button at line 30-32 so the screen has one forward action.

title: Clients get no notification badge on desktop — the bell is buried in the account menu
surface: Client portal, any page: desktop left rail (bottom) versus mobile top bar
whatYouSee: On a phone there is a bell with a count in the top bar. On a desktop the bell exists only as a "Notifications" row inside the account dropdown at the bottom of the rail, and the count is only visible once that dropdown is open. Nothing on the visible page hints that drafts are waiting for review.
whyItsWrong: The point of a badge is ambient signal. A client with items sitting in "Ready for review" sees nothing until they happen to click their own avatar, so approvals stall and the portal looks idle. Staff get a permanently visible bell in the workspace header, so the two shells behave differently for no reason a client can see.

If the row must stay, compute the same total and mirror it onto the AccountMenu trigger (account-menu.tsx:64) as a dot so the count is visible without opening the menu.

title: No admin surface shows any client's credit balance, yet every denial tells the client to "ask your Karos team"
surface: Admin Clients list /clients and Admin Analytics /admin/analytics
whatYouSee: The Clients grid shows each brand with asset and job counts — no credits. Admin Analytics shows model cost in dollars, tokens, runs, errors, logins and feedback — no credits. To learn that a client is out of credits an admin must open that one client's Settings page and scroll to the Credits card. There is no list, no sort, no low-balance flag, no alert.
whyItsWrong: The client-facing wall says to ask the Karos team for a top-up, and the copilot is instructed to say the same below 20 credits — but the Karos team has no queue, no notification and no dashboard telling them who is asking. The only credit-granting control in the product is inside a single client's settings page, so the remedy for every credit denial is an out-of-band conversation the portal neither triggers nor records. A client can sit blocked indefinitely while the agency's own analytics page reports everything green.

Then add a "Clients low on credits" block to src/app/(app)/admin/analytics/page.tsx using the same helper, so the agency sees the ask before the client has to send an email.

title: The Connect page promises "submit managed jobs" and walks through an Instagram job the MCP server has no tool for
whatYouSee: The page header says Karos exposes an MCP server your Claude Code can use to "read client data, browse jobs & assets, submit managed jobs, and upload files." Step 3 gives the worked example: "submit a 3-post Instagram job focused on their summer launch and tell me the job id", then states Claude Code will read the client's context and submit the managed job to the agent service. A staff member follows it and Claude Code reports there is no such tool.
whyItsWrong: The server exposes twelve tools and the only one that starts work runs a repo agent with a prompt. There is no submit-managed-job tool. The page's own "Available tools" sidebar confirms it — it lists the run-a-repo-agent tool and says nothing about managed jobs. So the headline promise and the worked example both describe a capability the server does not have, and the two halves of the same page contradict each other.

Either add a submit_managed_job tool to src/lib/mcp/tools.ts wrapping submitManagedJob from src/lib/jobs/submit-managed.ts (same pattern as run_agent at tools.ts:312; the core already takes an AppUser, so PAT auth works) and add it to the sidebar array at src/app/(app)/connect/page.tsx:75-86 — or rewrite connect/page.tsx line 20 and lines 62-68 to describe running a repo agent with a prompt, which is what actually happens. Either way fix the stale comment at src/lib/actions/external-job-actions.ts:12, which names a tool that does not exist.

title: The smallest type in the portal sits below the accessibility contrast floor in 143 places
surface: Whole portal (every card caption, meta line, stat sub-label, timestamp)
whatYouSee: The ten and eleven pixel supporting text everywhere — the sub-labels under the analytics headline numbers, the per-million pricing in the model table, the coverage lines under the search score tiles, relative timestamps on run rows, platform descriptions on channel cards, the "plus three more" in calendar cells — is a mid grey that visibly fades into the card behind it, especially on a laptop screen at an angle or in daylight.
whyItsWrong: The dim grey against the card surface computes to roughly 3.5 to 1, under the 4.5 to 1 floor for normal-size text — and these are the smallest sizes in the app, so the large-text exemption does not apply. The token is used 463 times, 143 of them on a line that also sets ten or eleven pixel type. The numbers and units that qualify every metric end up the hardest things on the page to read. Light mode is no better, at roughly 3.6 to 1.

title: The three agent pages print the raw database job status "review" to clients, when the portal already has a label map that says "In review"
surface: X agent / LinkedIn agent / Reddit agent → Feedback card, recent-runs list (/clients/[id]/x-agent, /linkedin-agent, /reddit-agent)
whatYouSee: A list of recent runs reading "Run 2026-07-24 · review", "Run 2026-07-22 · queued", "Run 2026-07-19 · delivered".
whyItsWrong: The status word is printed exactly as it is stored. "review" is not a sentence and not a state a client can interpret, and the same underlying state is displayed as "In review" everywhere else in the portal (dashboard, jobs list, job detail) by the shared status badge. The value is typed as a plain string on the way to the screen, so nothing catches the mismatch.

title: Dismissing a "new content ready" notification only hides it until the next page load
surface: Notifications bell → "New content ready: …" row → X
whatYouSee: You click the X on a content-ready notification, tooltip "Dismiss". It disappears and the count drops. Navigate anywhere, or let the page refresh, and it is back with the count restored.
whyItsWrong: The handler only writes to in-page state — there is no server call and nothing is stored. The identical-looking X on meeting action items right below does reach the server and sticks, so the two behave differently for no visible reason and the badge stops being trustworthy.

title: Platform names are title-cased from their ids: “Linkedin”, “Youtube”

title: Every notification is truncated mid-sentence and none of them are notifications
whatYouSee: Both rows read as cut-off task descriptions: “Provide feedback on the Instagram agent UI and output quality after the…” and “Work with Yair to have all product agents ready and integrated on the…”, each stamped “Portal final sprint · 19d ago”. The panel footer says “View all meetings →”.
whyItsWrong: These are internal task rows surfaced as notifications, cut mid-sentence, under a footer that links to meetings. Nothing here tells the reader what happened or what to do, and a 19-day-old item is still presented as active.

fix: Write notifications as events with a subject and a verb (“Instagram agent run failed · 9h ago”), let them wrap to two lines instead of clipping, point the footer at whatever the rows actually are, and age out or visually de-emphasise anything older than a week.

title: The Meetings list is not in date order — synced meetings land wherever the sync ran
whatYouSee: Live right now, top to bottom: Jun 21 → Jun 23 → 7h ago → 4h ago → 8d ago → 7d ago. On the call: "Why is it not in order?" — noticed the moment three freshly synced meetings appeared above newer ones.
whyItsWrong: The list is sorted by createdAt — the moment the record was synced into Firestore — not by when the meeting happened. Fireflies backfills insert old meetings at the top, and the type already carries the real meetingDate field the sort ignores.
evidence: src/lib/data.ts:769–784 — listTranscripts sorts (b.createdAt ?? 0) − (a.createdAt ?? 0)
src/lib/types.ts:1016 — meetingDate?: number exists on Transcript
src/app/(app)/transcripts/page.tsx — no re-sort after fetch
fix: Sort by (meetingDate ?? createdAt) descending in listTranscripts, and show meetingDate on the row when present so the displayed date is the one being sorted. One line plus a display touch.
